notes: Central air conditioners and heat pumps (split systems — outdoor condenser/heat pump + indoor air handler/evaporator coil). NOT furnaces, NOT mini-splits/ductless, NOT packaged/rooftop units, NOT window units. The outdoor unit is the scored product. Scored by compressor technology (single/two-stage/variable-speed), efficiency (SEER2/HSPF2), construction quality, and serviceability.

tier_anchors.notes: Carrier Infinity: Greenspeed Intelligence, Copeland variable-speed scroll, communicating system, fewest contractor callbacks among premium lines. Yale/CR data consistent. Trane XV: TruComfort variable-speed, Copeland (or Climatuff), robust build quality, most forgiving of installation quality. Both consensus Tier 1 from HVAC professionals.

Lennox SL28XCV: Industry-leading 28 SEER2, quietest operation, proprietary communicating system. Technologically superior but proprietary ecosystem creates service/parts premium (15-20% above Carrier/Trane). Contractors acknowledge best-in-class specs but steer some buyers away due to total cost of ownership. Tier 2 due to service ecosystem limitation.

Rheem Prestige: Reliable mid-tier (Toyota Camry of HVAC per contractor consensus). Superior to Goodman in build quality and longevity. Open parts ecosystem. Goodman GSXC18: Daikin-owned since 2012 — meaningfully improved quality vs pre-acquisition. Widest parts availability (GEMAIRE, Ferguson, Johnstone Supply). Strong value. Both represent the floor for 'acceptable in a quality home' per professional consensus (16+ SEER2, two-stage minimum).

Builder-grade floor. Single-stage, fixed orifice. High-volume new construction standard ($300K-600K tract homes). 8-10 year expected lifespan per repair tech consensus. Functional but no differentiation. Parts universally available. Represents the floor that every buyer should know about.

No calibration products. Reserved for brands with no US service infrastructure, active safety recalls, or documented structural defects. MRCOOL DIY potentially here if research confirms professional concerns.

quality.notes: THE key differentiator in HVAC — equivalent of cartridge for faucets. Variable-speed (Copeland ZPD, Daikin inverter): precise capacity modulation, 25-100% output, best comfort/efficiency. Two-stage: 67%/100% steps, good comfort. Single-stage: on/off only, short-cycling in oversized installs.

Copeland (Emerson/Copeland) dominates residential market >60%. Copeland scroll = industry standard, proven lifespan. Daikin compressors in Daikin Fit/DX lines. Unknown/undisclosed = risk. Bristol/NIDEC adequate but lower market credibility.

CRITICAL finding from research: microchannel coils have 4-5x shorter lifespan than traditional copper/aluminum. Carrier switched some lines to microchannel. Trane Spine Fin is different construction. Traditional copper/aluminum is most repairable and durable.
EEV: precise metering, required for true variable-speed optimal performance. TXV: standard for two-stage and premium single-stage. Fixed orifice: budget, less efficient, more charge-sensitive.
Variable-speed BLDC: 75%+ efficiency, quietest. ECM: 65-75% efficiency, standard premium. PSC: 40-50% efficiency, builder-grade, higher energy, noisier.
Cabinet quality affects outdoor unit longevity. Heavy gauge with proper powder coat and louvered fin protection = premium. Light gauge with mesh guard = budget.
Lennox: proprietary platform (+1). Carrier: Charlotte NC identified factories (+1). Trane: Tyler TX (+1). Goodman: Houston TX (+1). Bristol compressor = identified. Unknown OEM = -1.

performance.notes: SEER2 (post-2023 DOE standard, more realistic than old SEER). Range: 13.4 (code minimum) to 28+ (Lennox SL28XCV top). Real-world spread significant. Lennox leads, Carrier/Trane competitive, builder-grade at minimum.
Heat pump heating efficiency. Only scored for heat pump products. AC-only: N/A. Range: 6.7 to 12+. Variable-speed units dominate top end.
Outdoor unit sound at rated conditions. Lennox as low as 56 dB. Premium variable-speed 58-65 dB. Standard single-stage 72-76 dB. Massive comfort impact for homeowner and neighbors.
Variable-speed 25-100% = best comfort (no short cycling, precise temp control, continuous dehumidification). Two-stage 67/100% = good. Single-stage on/off = worst comfort.
Heat pump only. Premium heat pumps operate to -13°F or below with maintained capacity. Mid-tier drops off significantly below 17°F. AC-only: N/A.

durability.notes: Industry standard: 10-year compressor warranty (with registration). Goodman/Amana: lifetime compressor (genuinely claimable post-Daikin). Lennox: 10-year. Short warranty = manufacturer confidence signal.
Parts warranty separate from compressor. Most premium: 10-year registered. Budget: 5-year.
Daikin/Goodman and Rheem rated most claim-friendly by contractors. Lennox rated most difficult due to proprietary requirements.

Goodman: widest availability (GEMAIRE, Ferguson, Johnstone). Carrier: Carrier Enterprise (some restriction). Lennox: highly proprietary (15-20% price premium, longer lead times). Parts availability directly impacts repair speed and cost.
Goodman/Rheem: serviced by any contractor. Carrier/Trane: certified dealer networks plus independents. Lennox: certified dealers preferred, proprietary diagnostics.

Some brands offer WeatherShield, Quantum coil, or similar coatings. Microchannel coils have documented higher corrosion rates in coastal/chemical environments (4-5x shorter lifespan). Traditional copper/aluminum without coating = standard.
Control boards are a leading failure mode. Communicating systems (Carrier Infinity, Trane ComfortLink, Lennox iComfort) add complexity. Research needed on brand-specific board failure rates.
R-410A being phased down (EPA 2025). R-454B (A2L mildly flammable) is next gen. Units sold 2025+ should be R-454B ready. R-22 is obsolete and service costs are prohibitive.

scoring_rules: Compressor type (variable-speed/two-stage/single-stage) is THE primary differentiator — equivalent of cartridge for faucets or motor for dishwashers.
Score the outdoor unit (condenser or heat pump). Indoor air handler scored as part of the system only if it meaningfully differentiates within a brand family.
Carrier/Bryant/Heil platform sharing: Carrier Infinity vs Bryant Evolution = same compressor, same board, different badge/thermostat ecosystem. Report must disclose. Score separately per Rule 19.
Trane/American Standard: Different product tiers within same parent (Johnson Controls). Not identical units at component level. Score separately.

Goodman/Amana/Daikin family: Post-2012 Daikin acquisition. Goodman and Amana are largely badge-engineered (same compressor, coil, different distributor channel). Daikin Fit/DX is separate platform. Report must disclose.
Rheem/Ruud: Same unit, different distribution channel. True badge engineering. Score Rheem, note Ruud identical.
York/Coleman/Luxaire (Johnson Controls): Badge-engineered from same platforms. Report must disclose.
Lennox proprietary ecosystem rule: Lennox proprietary distribution and communicating system create higher total cost of ownership. This is a durability/serviceability finding, NOT a quality finding.
Microchannel coil rule: If brand uses microchannel coils, apply -1 condenser coil adjustment AND note 4-5x shorter lifespan in report.
Installation sensitivity rule: HVAC performance is 80% installation quality. Top brands (Trane, Carrier) most forgiving of mediocre installs. Note installation sensitivity in report for all products.
Heat pump vs AC-only: Heat pump products score HSPF2 and cold weather performance. AC-only products: those fields are N/A (Rule 16).
Refrigerant transition rule: Note R-410A vs R-454B status. Buyer needs to know future refrigerant cost implications.
MRCOOL/DIY rule: If product sold as DIY installation, note professional consensus on DIY HVAC reliability in report.
